queries.name: simulator-database-inputs
queries.subject: Model daily run volume and 30-day retained detail from user-supplied scenario inputs.
queries.objective: Compare hypothetical workload choices without treating results as observed activity.
queries.acceptance: Each simulated day uses the selected inputs; skipped runs retain summaries and detailed records have a 30-day lifetime.
queries.description: Each simulated day includes all accumulated run summaries; tools and issues belong only to non-skipped runs and expire after 30 days.

queries.name: simulator-run-size
queries.subject: Estimate retained run-summary table size at 512 bytes per run.
queries.objective: Show modeled accumulation of run summaries.
queries.acceptance: Summary size includes every simulated run at 512 bytes and is not presented as measured storage.

queries.name: simulator-tool-size
queries.subject: Estimate retained tool table size at 256 bytes per tool on non-skipped runs.
queries.objective: Show modeled tool-record growth under the selected workload.
queries.acceptance: Tool size uses only non-skipped simulated runs and 256 bytes per tool over the retained period.

queries.name: simulator-issue-size
queries.subject: Estimate retained issue table size at 512 bytes per issue on non-skipped runs.
queries.objective: Show modeled issue-record growth under the selected workload.
queries.acceptance: Issue size uses only non-skipped simulated runs and 512 bytes per issue over the retained period.

queries.name: simulator-database-size
queries.subject: Show modeled run-summary, tool, and issue table bytes after 30 days.
queries.objective: Compare hypothetical database table sizes at the end of the retention horizon.
queries.acceptance: The model presents separate summary, tool, and issue estimates after 30 simulated days, never observed storage.
queries.description: Run summaries accumulate; detailed records have a 30-day TTL.

queries.name: simulator-database-total
queries.subject: Sum the modeled table sizes after 30 days.
queries.objective: Show the final estimated size of the modeled database tables.
queries.acceptance: The final value is the sum of the three modeled table sizes after 30 days.

queries.name: simulator-database-summary
queries.subject: List modeled table sizes and their final total after 30 days.
queries.objective: Present the 30-day estimate in a compact table.
queries.acceptance: Three modeled table sizes and their summed final value are shown without a growth chart.

queries.name: simulator-pr-inputs
queries.subject: Model company PR volume, AW fan-out and AI Credits from editable assumptions.
queries.objective: Compare hypothetical company sizes without launching workflows or claiming measured capacity.
queries.acceptance: Developers multiply PRs per developer per day, AW runs per PR and AIC per run; repositories divide averages only. Duration scales totals independently of the synthetic day source.

queries.name: simulator-pr-counts
queries.subject: Show modeled daily and horizon pull request counts.
queries.objective: Separate developer activity from repository scope.
queries.acceptance: PR totals depend on developers and duration, not repository count.

queries.name: simulator-pr-runs
queries.subject: Show modeled AW runs generated by pull requests.
queries.acceptance: Daily and horizon runs use the configured AW runs per PR.

queries.name: simulator-pr-aic
queries.subject: Show modeled AI Credits, not actual spending or currency.
queries.objective: Make the editable AIC-per-run assumption explicit.
queries.acceptance: AIC totals multiply modeled runs by AIC per AW run; no dollar conversion or budget enforcement is inferred.

queries.name: simulator-pr-summary
queries.subject: Compare daily and horizon PR, AW-run and AI Credit estimates.
queries.acceptance: Exactly three modeled measures are shown and recompute from all six form inputs.

pages.intent: Explore modeled database growth under the declared retention and workload assumptions.
pages.subject: Synthetic growth estimates from the selected simulator inputs and 30-day detail retention.
pages.objective: Compare capacity scenarios, not predict observed production performance.
pages.acceptance: Show input assumptions, modeled horizon and size/count units; recompute on parameter changes. Clearly distinguish estimates from measurements and do not infer actual storage use or capacity guarantees.
pages.title: Simulators
pages.description: Compare modeled storage capacity under the selected CAO workload assumptions.

form.title: Database size
form.description: Set a hypothetical daily workload. Skipped runs retain summaries but produce no tools or issues.

views.title: Database size after 30 days
views.subject: Estimated retained size of run, tool, and issue tables.
views.objective: Compare hypothetical table growth under different workload and skip-rate inputs.
views.acceptance: Three modeled table sizes after 30 days and their final total use the authored byte-per-record assumptions, with run summaries retained and detailed records limited to 30 days; no value is presented as observed storage.
views.description: Modeled data size, not measured storage: 512 bytes per run summary or issue and 256 bytes per tool. Run summaries persist; tool and issue records expire after 30 days. Indexes, metadata, compression, and other tables are excluded.

pages.intent: Explore PR-driven company workloads with editable AW and AIC assumptions.
pages.subject: Hypothetical pull requests, AW runs and AI Credits for the selected company size and duration.
pages.objective: Compare workload volume, not predict observed throughput or spending.
pages.acceptance: All six inputs are editable and recompute daily and horizon totals. Repositories affect averages only. No agents, stress tests, GitHub actions or spending are triggered.
pages.title: Pull request simulator
pages.description: Compare modeled PR, AW-run and AI Credit totals without launching workflows, running stress tests or spending credits.

form.title: Company workload
form.description: PRs are per developer per day, not per repository. Duration counts calendar days. The CLI stress runner independently bounds generated records to five million.

views.title: Modeled daily and horizon totals
views.subject: Synthetic PR, AW-run and AI Credit counts.
views.objective: Compare daily activity with the selected duration.
views.acceptance: Counts use the selected assumptions; AIC is modeled credits, not measured billing or currency.
views.description: Daily PRs = developers × PRs/developer/day. AW runs = PRs × AW runs/PR. AI Credits = AW runs × AIC/run. Horizon totals multiply daily values by the selected duration.

views.subject: Daily per-repository and per-second workload averages.
views.objective: Explain how repository count distributes the same developer workload.
views.acceptance: Averages are not peak traffic, measured throughput, storage predictions or capacity guarantees.
views.description: Uniform averages over repositories and 86,400 seconds per day. Bursts, execution duration, retries and storage overhead are excluded.
